scope: The TOPP -threads parameter: how many workers a tool run may use, and that the setting reaches the run phase of the five ported tools. Sources come from the OpenMS4-cli package, which is versioned independently of the Core SDK and is therefore not listed in current_sdk_reference_manifests.
method: TOPPBase::setMaxNumberOfThreads and its call site were read at the cli pin. The semantics were then executed against the optimised C++ Release build openms4-release-bc9cc12-c19e494-174b576 (oracle/release-build/manifest.json) on ibminode06: MapNormalizer and (for the pair comparison on dax) DTAExtractor were run on the benchmark's derived UK222 slices while /proc/<pid>/task was sampled every millisecond, recording the most tasks seen at once, how many of them accumulated CPU time, and when each count first appeared. Cases vary -threads (1, 4, 16, 0, -1, -7), OMP_NUM_THREADS (unset, 1, 16), the CPU affinity mask (taskset -c 0-3) and the phase (-write_ini, which never reaches main_). The start-up threads that appear without OMP_NUM_THREADS were attributed with gdb: a breakpoint on pthread_create shows blas_thread_init in the conda-forge liblapack.so.3 (OpenBLAS) during dynamic-loader initialisation, not OpenMS code. The same probe was then run against the Rust release binaries of this branch on dax, for the same inputs and settings.
evidence_tier: executed differential (tier 1 probe) against the C++ Release build for the -threads semantics and the thread counts; tier 4 (native invariants) for the pool size observed inside the port and for output equality across worker counts
